- When sentiment is consistently positive (≥0.20) over recent days, model tends to overestimate prices; reduce forecast peak by 5–10% in subsequent periods.
- If model shows sharp upward spike followed by forecast decline, true price often rebounds — adjust downward forecast only if sentiment remains neutral or negative.
- In high-sentiment periods, model underestimates late-period price peaks; add 3–5% buffer to final 5–7 days of forecast.
- If model forecast mean is significantly below true outcome mean (e.g., >10% gap), check sentiment history for recent positive momentum — if present, increase forecast baseline by 2–5%.
- Model often underreacts to sentiment shifts — if sentiment turns positive mid-period, adjust forecast upward by 1–3% per day until sentiment stabilizes.
- For 30-day forecasts, model tends to overfit recent trends; apply 1–2 day lag correction: forecast day 10–15 should be 5–10% below true outcome if sentiment is neutral or declining.
- If sentiment is negative (≤0.10) and model forecasts are rising, reduce forecast by 5–10% to avoid overcorrection.
- Model frequently misses mean-reversion tail — if price has risen >15% from 10-day average, forecast should taper downward by 1–2% per day for next 3–5 days unless sentiment supports continuation.
